# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: SW-MES-01 (Simulated)
- Period: week 9 (starting 2026-03-02)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift found that this clinic's scans no longer look like the scans the AI was validated on (drift score 0.99, where 0.5 means like training and 1 clearly different).
Its catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) therefore cannot be verified from 50 scans from this week, and expert grades for these scans have not yet arrived. The AI is referring more patients than usual: 86% of this week's scans, against 68% of the training scans.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of possibly missed cases is not estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Changes in image quality and camera hardware configuration leading to lower contrast and sharpness, impacting referral rates (category: camera or image quality; confidence 95%; source: gemini).

Evidence:
- Drift score is 0.99, indicating scans no longer look like training data.
- Mean quality dropped from 0.5 to 0.193, a relative change of -0.614.
- Mean contrast decreased from 0.0963 to 0.0548, a relative change of -0.431.
- Mean sharpness decreased from 0.000399 to 0.000222, a relative change of -0.443.
- Mean resolution increased from 1020.0 px to 2070.0 px, a relative change of 1.019.
- Referral rate increased from 0.685 to 0.86, a relative change of 0.256.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI at this clinic because its scans have drifted beyond what the AI was validated on, so its catch rate cannot be verified. We recommend sending this clinic's scans for human grading until the checks below are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect the camera hardware and clean the lenses.
- [ ] Verify camera capture settings and check if resolution scaling or compression algorithms were altered.
- [ ] Review technician imaging protocols to ensure proper focus, alignment, and illumination.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
